findings.title: The garden as a material credential
findings.claim: The focus specifies a garden for the addressee, names its date palms and grapes, and demands rivers burst through its interstices. In 25:8 a privately held garden that can be eaten from is placed among the conditions opponents attach to following a messenger. That wider contact makes the focus's working orchard read as a material credential, while 25:10 frames gardens and rivers as contingent gifts, 16:67 gives the crops divergent uses, and 76:6 places forcefully opened water in a drinking scene.
findings.mechanism: The focus garden and its crop and water words carry the owned productive system; 25:8 independently links a private garden to a messenger-status demand, so the focus's for-you ownership and active river-making become a test of material authority. The conditional gift in 25:10 and the use-scenes in 16:67 and 76:6 meet the same crops and flow, changing the reading from undifferentiated abundance to an owned proof-object whose yield and water also have contingent, practical uses.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see the specific form of the demand: not abundance in the abstract, but a personally held orchard and a water network treated as evidence, with the same materials remaining legible as contingent provision and usable resources.
findings.containment: The focus remains a demand, not a report that the garden is granted or that it proves authority. The wider ayat are contextual parallels, not identical scenes; their target morphology is not supplied, and their uses do not settle the focus demand.

epistemic.reason: The cross-run support is trusted and citable, and the focus carriers resolve completely to QAC. The additional reader and HFT summaries are legacy-unbound nominations; the external connection rows supply exact Arabic surfaces but not target morphology, so the contextual contacts remain qualified.

findings.title: A garden as a water-landscape
findings.claim: The focus places rivers through the garden's interstices. In 27:61, rivers are placed through the earth's interstices; the wider echo makes this garden a compressed water-landscape, so the requested private asset takes on the geometry of a broader ordered terrain.
findings.mechanism: The focus garden and خِلَٰلَهَا carry the enclosed place and its passages; the separate river word supplies what moves through them. The exact 27:61 surface joins interstices and rivers at the scale of the earth, and that independent pattern returns through the focus's خِلَٰلَهَا relation, changing the orchard from a crop enclosure into a small-scale channel landscape.
findings.reader_payoff: The wording locates water inside the garden's intervals, while the wider parallel makes that arrangement perceptible as a scaled landscape pattern.
findings.containment: This is a structural echo, not a claim that both passages describe the same event or agent, and not an assertion that 17:91 describes the earth itself. The 27:61 target morphology is not supplied.

findings.title: A productive garden is not secure control
findings.claim: The focus's garden and rivers can be read alongside wider garden-owner scenes in which confidence in an orchard's permanence meets its loss, and a matching palm-and-grape river garden is consumed by fire. The desired asset remains a sign of abundance, while its security becomes uncertain.
findings.mechanism: The focus garden is the carrier. In 18:35 its owner says he does not expect his garden to perish, and 18:42 records its ruin; 2:266 repeats palms, grapes, and rivers before a whirlwind with fire consumes the orchard. These independent wider scenes return through the focus garden and water network, changing ownership from a guarantee of control into a vulnerable condition.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hold the appeal of a richly productive garden together with the possibility that possession and irrigation do not make it permanent.
findings.containment: These are separate scenes, not predictions that the focus garden will burn or a moral diagnosis of its addressee. Their target-side morphology is not supplied.

epistemic.reason: The focus branches and the external Arabic surfaces are supplied, and the garden-loss relation is explicit in those contexts. The connection rows do not supply target morphology, so the cross-ayah comparison remains qualified.
